findings.finding: Application runs on a single EC2 instance with no auto-scaling, load balancing, or high availability
Static files served from local disk with no CDN integration
Database co-located on the same instance as the application server — no separation of concerns
No environment-based configuration — secrets and settings hardcoded in source
No health check endpoints for load balancer or orchestrator integration
SMTP dependency on on-premises Exchange server prevents cloud-native messaging
No use of managed services (SQS, SNS, SES, ElastiCache) for common patterns
Python 2.7 runtime is not available in modern container base images — migration to Python 3.x required first
System-wide package installation (no virtualenv) — dependency isolation not established
Apache + mod_wsgi deployment model requires rearchitecting to a WSGI/ASGI server suitable for containers
No Dockerfile, docker-compose, or container configuration exists
Application stores state on local filesystem (static files) — not container-friendly
No requirements.txt with pinned, reproducible dependencies for container builds
Python 2.7 and Django 1.4 are end-of-life — no longer receiving community security patches or updates
PostgreSQL 9.1 is end-of-life — must upgrade to a supported version (15+)
Ubuntu 12.04 and Apache 2.2 are end-of-life — no community support
Already uses open-source stack (Python, Django, PostgreSQL) — no proprietary vendor lock-in
Database runs on the same EC2 instance as the application — no managed service, no replication, no automated failover
Only backup is a daily pg_dump cron job — no point-in-time recovery, no automated backup management
Database credentials hardcoded in source code — no IAM authentication or secrets management integration
PostgreSQL 9.1 is end-of-life — incompatible with current Amazon RDS minimum supported versions
Raw SQL queries with no ORM usage — increases migration risk due to potential PostgreSQL version-specific SQL syntax
Single database with simple schema — migration complexity is low once version upgrade is complete
No analytics or reporting capabilities exist — ticket data is only accessible via the two view endpoints
No data export, ETL pipeline, or data warehouse integration
No logging infrastructure that could feed analytics systems
Simple relational schema could be easily exported to analytics services
No CI/CD pipeline — deployment is manual git pull + Apache restart
No automated testing — only stale unit tests mentioned in README
No infrastructure as code — server configuration is manual and undocumented
SECRET_KEY and database password committed to source control — no secrets management
DEBUG = True in production — no environment separation or configuration management
No code quality gates, linting, or static analysis
No monitoring, alerting, or incident management integration
Source code is in git — version control foundation exists
No machine-readable API — AI/ML services cannot integrate programmatically
No structured logging or event data to train ML models on ticket patterns
SQL injection vulnerabilities make any automated system integration dangerous
No webhook or event-driven architecture for AI service triggers
Ticket data locked in legacy database with no export pipeline for ML training
Helpdesk domain is well-suited for AI (auto-classification, suggested responses, sentiment analysis)

critical_security_findings.finding: SQL injection via string formatting in database queries
Cross-site scripting (XSS) via unsanitized HTML output
Database password committed to source control in plaintext
DEBUG = True in production exposes stack traces
